messages:
maria: quick heads-up, ran a full nsys + perfetto pass on the prod-like load (kv-cache enabled, batcher=adaptive) — I see periodic cudaMalloc spikes aligned with some kernel selector changes 
aj: can you paste the slice or timeline? which kernels are toggling at those moments?
sophie: fwiw last week we saw similar spikes when the batcher switched to small-batch mode, might be related to ephemeral KV cache growth
maria: attaching condensed timeline snippet from nsys (i trimmed noise):
```
Time   Event
0.0s   kernel: attn_fused_1 (fastpath)
0.2s   kernel: matmul_large
0.21s  cudaMalloc(24MB) spike
0.21s  kernel: attn_generic (fallback slowpath)
0.32s  kernel: kv_cache_store
0.33s  cudaFree
0.35s  kernel: attn_fused_1
```

maria: spike coincides with kernel falling back from fused fastpath to generic attn; suspect fallback path allocates temporary buffers into device heap
devon: do we have a per-request sequence-length distribution? fallback could trigger for long sequences or for attention types with unsupported stride
aj: i pulled perfetto heap-alloc heatmap — highest allocation density on stream 4 during those windows. sample file: gs://redwood-perf/nsys/1901234567/heap-heatmap.pb
sophie: interesting — also saw that our arena slab sizes are 8MB by default. if the fallback requests a ~12MB scratch we end up invoking cudaMalloc instead of suballocating
maria: exact. hypothesis: kernel selector switches to generic that expects a contiguous scratch > slab size, so pool returns NULL and we call cudaMalloc async which spikes
aj: can you repro with smaller synthetic workload? maybe force the selector to choose generic path via env var MODEL_ATTENTION_MODE=generic and run nsys with --trace-memory
maria: did that. with MODEL_ATTENTION_MODE=generic i get lots of cudaMallocAsync calls at ~0.18s and fragmentation grows over time in arena snapshots

perf-bot: new perf run uploaded: /runs/1901234567-generic-attn-nsys.log

maria: i compared two runs: (A) adaptive batcher triggering small batches => more fallbacks => more allocs, (B) fixed large-batch config => fewer fallbacks and stable arena
sophie: so short-term mitigation: increase slab size to 16MB and enable deferred free batching (we already have a flag POOL_FREE_DELAY_MS)
devon: cautious: increasing slab size reduces fragmentation but may increase resident set for many concurrent contexts — need quota guard for dedicated pools
aj: another angle: change kernel selector to prefer fused fastpath when input dims are within X range even if some heuristics suggest generic; fallback cost > correctness? any functional differences?
maria: functionally identical, just different memory contract. i'll open a small patch to bias selector for < 2048 seq length toward fused where possible
sophie: also add a fast allocation path: if required_scratch <= slab_size * 2, try two-slab contiguous allocation attempt before calling cudaMalloc; cheap but reduces calling into device allocator
devon: let's capture a perf delta: run a 30m soak with slab=16MB + deferred-free=200ms + selector-bias and compare token-per-second and 95p latency

aj: note for the soak: enable kv_cache prefix caching off for first run to isolate kv_cache growth effects
maria: command I used to repro locally:
```
MODEL_ATTENTION_MODE=generic POOL_SLAB_SIZE_MB=8 POOL_FREE_DELAY_MS=0 ./bin/serve --profile nsys --trace perfetto://heap.pb --batcher adaptive --workload replay/longseq.json
```
maria: and with mitigations:
```
MODEL_ATTENTION_MODE=auto POOL_SLAB_SIZE_MB=16 POOL_FREE_DELAY_MS=200 ./bin/serve --profile nsys --trace perfetto://heap2.pb --batcher adaptive --workload replay/longseq.json
```

perf-bot: summary metrics uploaded: /runs/1901234567/summary.json (shows 22% reduction in cudaMalloc count and 9% lower p95 latency in mitigated run)

aj: sounds promising. next steps: mariap to send a patch for selector-bias + two-slab attempt; sophie to prototype automated slab-size recommendation based on observed scratch quantiles; devon to validate memory impact under heavy concurrency
maria: will do the selector patch and add a CLI flag to aggressively prefer fused for small seqs; i'll also include a perf test script that produces the nsys slice and heap snapshots automatically
sophie: i'll write a small analyzer that scans perfetto heap snapshots and emits quantiles for scratch allocations, then surface a suggested POOL_SLAB_SIZE_MB in the console optimizer
devon: i'll run a dedicated cluster run tomorrow with 200 concurrent streams and report resident set impact

aj: great. if anyone hits this in the wild, quick triage checklist: 1) check nsys timeline for attn fallback patterns 2) correlate with cudaMalloc spikes 3) inspect arena slab utilization 4) repro with MODEL_ATTENTION_MODE=generic
maria: adding that to runbook under eng-runtime/perf-runbook.md (will PR)
aj: :thumbsup:
